utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-01-42/2-I, the Prosecutor versus Vladimir Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. And good afternoon to everyone before this recomposed Chamber in this case. Judge Moloto has joined us and has replaced Judge El Mahdi. May I have the appearances? Prosecution first.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Susan L. Somers, senior trial attorney. To my immediate left, David Re, trial attorney, to my right case manager Helena Tavares-Borges. Behind me, as for the Prosecution staff, Mr. Phillip Weiner, trial attorney, and Mr. Aleksandar Kontic, trial attorney.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: There are, of course, other people sitting at counsel table. Will the Chamber take the initiative or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll take the initiative. If these are experts, I'll try to find out where the experts are and how many there are. Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. For Mr. Vladimir Kovacevic, Tanja Radosavljevic, Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Radosavljevic. As far as the order of this afternoon is concerned, I suggest to the parties the following. At the beginning, I'd like to ask all experts that have appeared and that have reported on the mental health of Mr. Kovacevic to make a solemn declaration, to confirm that they did write their reports to the best of their abilities, and having given this solemn declaration, I would like to invite the parties to put any additional questions to experts, whether it be experts called by themselves or called by the other party, and to do that in approximately 45 minutes first round. Then we have a break. And on the basis of the answers given by the experts, the Chamber may have some additional questions as well, and the parties will have another possibility responding to what the experts have told us to put more questions to the experts in approximately 25 to 30 minutes. So altogether, that would be 75 minutes for each party. The logical order in my view would be that if you have any questions to -- Yes, your microphone is on. Perhaps it's better to -- To start putting questions to your own expert or, and only at the very last, to put questions to the expert of the other party. What we could do, actually, is to split up even the first 45 minutes and give an opportunity to Prosecution and Defence to first put the questions to either the Court's experts or the experts called by themselves, and then after you have done that, then to put any questions to the expert called by the other party. So please split up your time as you deem fit for the first 45 minutes. We will keep some record on that. If you would, for example, use 15 minutes to put additional questions to your own expert, you would have 30 minutes remaining for experts called by the other party. That's what I suggest to the parties. If there is any comment on that, or any disagreement, I would like to hear it now. And let's not forget the Chamber has read all the reports. There is no need whatsoever to solicit from the experts what they have put on paper already. Is that clear?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Just a brief mention that yesterday, perhaps it was explained to us somewhat differently so we prepared more for full examination of ours. We weren't sure if the 75 minutes were to include cross. It wasn't really broken down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. As a matter of fact, we leave it entirely up to you. If you say the reports of my expert are perfectly clear, the only thing I wish to do is to cross-examine the experts of the other party on their reports and when the cross-examination by, for example, the Defence would raise any need to put additional questions in chief to my expert, you could do that in the second portion of 30 minutes. So I leave it up to you, whether you would seek to clarify your own position primarily, or whether you would want to challenge the expertise of the other party, and therefore, it's -- where you put the emphasis is entirely up to you. You may use your 75 minutes as you deem fit.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: May we inquire, does the Chamber plan to ask any additional questions of the court experts, so we know at the time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We may have some questions for the -- perhaps for all experts. But, of course, if you have put already all the relevant questions, we might have less questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll try to adapt to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's -- let's see whether we can proceed. Ms. Radosavljevic, any comments on the order proposed?

utterances.speaker: MS. RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: I understand that this is actually a ruling of the Trial Chamber that we have to keep in this time frame.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we have to finish today. Of course, after you have both spent 75 minutes, once we have put questions to the experts, if there is any time remaining then, of course, we could use that to the benefit of the Court, but we have reserved this afternoon for this hearing.

utterances.speaker: MS. RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. There is another issue that I was just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I cannot say briefly address to the Chamber, but I think I have to. Namely, the Defence moves the Chamber to in total disregard the medical expertise submitted by the Prosecution for the following reasons. The Prosecution has put in a motion for reconsideration of the order from the 7th October 2005 to obtain further medical examination. We all know, and I won't keep us very long, what the demand in this motion was. This motion was denied by the Trial Chamber. Afterwards, the Prosecution put in a request for certification which was also --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Denied.

utterances.speaker: MS. RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: -- dismissed on the 3rd of November 2005. I have received a complete B/C/S and English version yesterday of the medical experts of the Prosecution, and my first impression -- actually, the confirmation of my previous impression when I just got the B/C/S version of this report was that the Office of the Prosecutor has actually given to their medical expert witness another set of questions which are not the same questions given to all the other experts that appear here in court. The Defence sees this as a try to -- although the Chamber on two occasions gave their ruling that the questions from the 7th October order are the one that they want answers for, the OTP in this manner find a way -- found a way to, let's say, in -- to put in their -- the questions that they wanted through a small door.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, I see this as, well, I don't want to say abuse of procedural rights of the parties but an unfair proceeding. And therefore, I ask -- I move the Chamber to disregard in total the medical report of the experts of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Somers, would you like to respond to that?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I already observed that -- and I think that's true for both the original and B/C/S to the extent that I can compare it and the English translation, that at least the questions asked, it says, please quote here the questions asked, marked as pages so and so in the attachment. So therefore in the report itself, the questions do not appear clearly.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may respond.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: On the 17th of November, the Office of the Prosecutor sent to the two expert witnesses the questions and the issue if I believe full awareness was the most contentious one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was the issue.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Right. It's in the -- I would be very happy to tender it to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I suggest that during the first break, you and Ms. Radosavljevic will have a look at what questions you have put to the experts, and then Ms. Radosavljevic, of course, the issue remains on whether the experts kept to the questions put to them but that's, of course, a different matter and, of course, you're free to argue that for that reason, or if you're not convinced by what Ms. Somers shows you, to persist in your request. The Chamber will not immediately decide on the matter so we'll continue and we'll consider your request.

utterances.speaker: MS. RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We will follow the guidelines that you've given us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Then I'd like to find a way of, first of all, to identify all the experts present. I've got a list. Usually we find the experts just in front of us. It's a bit complicated today but I think we'll manage. I would like to know whether Mrs. Folnegovic is present.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please push the button of your microphone?

utterances.speaker: DR. FOLNEGOVIC-SMALC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Folnegovic, I'd like you -- because questions may be put to you, therefore I'd like you to make a solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth when you answer to those questions. The text is now handed out to you by the usher. Would you -- may I invite to you make that solemn declaration?

utterances.speaker: DR. FOLNEGOVIC-SMALC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Folnegovic. Please be seated. Then Danijela Zakic is present as well.

utterances.speaker: DR. ZAKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You've heard the procedure followed. I would like to invite you as well to make a solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: DR. ZAKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please be seated. Ana Najman, is she present? Yes, Ms. Najman, may I invite you also to make a solemn declaration?

utterances.speaker: DR. NAJMAN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Ms. Najman. Vladimir Ortakov.

utterances.speaker: DR. ORTAKOV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I am present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. May I also invite you to make a solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth?

utterances.speaker: DR. ORTAKOV
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ortakov. Then Mr. Blagojevic. Is Mr. Blagojevic present?

utterances.speaker: DR. BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then Ms. Dunja Krajinovic.

utterances.speaker: DR. KRAJINOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And finally, Mr. Goreta.

utterances.speaker: DR. GORETA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. May I put one general question to all of the experts present? We have received reports -- let me first concentrate on the report from Professor Folnegovic and Professor Zakic. Have you written these reports to the best of your professional abilities and in full accordance with the truth? May I ask you to confirm if you did so?

utterances.speaker: DR. FOLNEGOVIC-SMALC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Ms. Folnegovic. For you, Ms. Zakic, the same question.

utterances.speaker: DR. ZAKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That also applies to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please be seated. You don't have to stand up all the time I put questions to you because it would be a fatiguing afternoon for you. For the Defence, Defence experts, I would say experts called by the Defence, because you're not experts for the Defence. You're experts to assist the Court, and that's true for all of the experts, to assist the Court in preparing and making the determinations this Court will have to make. Ms. Najman, is it -- did you also make your report in accordance with the best of your professional abilities and in accordance with truth? Could you please bush the button of the microphone if you answer my question.

utterances.speaker: DR. NAJMAN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Absolutely in accordance with my knowledge, I drafted the report that was provided to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And the same question to you, Mr. Ortakov.

utterances.speaker: DR. ORTAKOV
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do see this is a confirmation of what I asked before. Then Mr. Blagojevic, you have not recently drafted a report but you have -- reports were presented on a regular basis. Were these reports made in accordance with your -- the best of your professional abilities and in accordance with the truth? Could you please push the button of your microphone if you answer my question.

utterances.speaker: DR. BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It's correct that I drafted the reports earlier and I sent them to you at regular intervals as requested. However, since August, I have not been sending these reports because, as of August the 1st, I am retired.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then Ms. Krajinovic, you have recently submitted a report on the request of the Chamber. Same question for you, whether it was drafted in accordance with the best of your professional abilities and in accordance with the truth. I see you nod -- yes.

utterances.speaker: DR. KRAJINOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All the expert reports so far drafted by myself and Dr. Goreta, so not only the most recent one but all the previous ones, were drafted in accordance with our professional knowledge and ethics which applies for forensic examinations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then the same question for you, Mr. Goreta, and also including all the previous reports, so not only the last one.

utterances.speaker: DR. GORETA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I drafted all the reports according to the criteria that you have referred to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Having received this confirmation, I would like to first give an opportunity to the Defence, unless the parties would have agreed otherwise, to use the first 30 minutes putting either additional -- 30 minutes -- no, let me say, to put those questions to the experts you called yourself. That would, for you, Ms. Radosavljevic, would be the report prepared by Ms. Najman, Mr. Ortakov, and also to experts called by the Chamber. That would be the report drafted by Ms. Krajinovic and Mr. Goreta, and if need be, also to the reports presented by Mr. Blagojevic and reserve your time for any questions you would like to put to the experts called by the Prosecution, that is Ms. Folnegovic and Ms. Zakic. So first up to you. We will just write down how much time you use. The remaining time of the 45 minutes in the first round, you can use to put questions at a later stage to the experts called by the Prosecution. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I plan to be very brief in the examination of my experts -- well, sorry, of the experts that I have called and that have presented a report. So are we going to proceed -- well, sorry, will they take the stand in the witness box or ...

utterances.speaker: MS. RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Or we can adapt our positions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apart from who is going to sit where, there is one remaining question, whether we are going to deal with all of this in open session, yes or no? That's an issue I should have raised, although not at the very beginning, because the public is certainly entitled to know what we are doing this afternoon. But since we do not know finally what the outcome, what the determination of the Chamber will be, I leave it to the parties, but especially to Ms. Radosavljevic, to consider whether or not she would like to go into private session because if Mr. Kovacevic would finally be found not to be fit to stand trial or to enter a plea, then it might be not a good idea to discuss the whole of his mental condition in a public hearing. There is always a possibility at a later stage if one of the parties applies to the Chamber, for making public what has been said in private session. We always then can consider to make it public. Ms. Radosavljevic, do you have any position in this respect?

utterances.speaker: MS. RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Well, as previously, the Defence is of the opinion that everything that has to do particularly with the diagnosis of Mr. Kovacevic and also any other material that could show to inform the people which diagnosis this actually is should go into a closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Somers, any objection?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution, as was the case in the Strugar case, which was held in open session, and again had a number of issues that, of course, involved issues that may be considered in a normal circumstance private but when the public interest is critical were deemed to be public, the Prosecution would move that the session in its entirety be open. If there are individual moments where closed session for any particular reason may be required, perhaps, but this, in our view, should be an open hearing in which the public has great interest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Somers, one of the problems is that once testimony is given in open session, it's very difficult to make it non-public afterwards. The other exercise, that is to make public what has been said in private session, is, of course, easier to do. But let me first consult with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Having heard the parties and having read the report, the Chamber prefers to hear the case in private session and leaves it open whether at a later stage there will be any need to make public what is not public today. Therefore, Mr. Registrar, would you --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I would like to -- I would like to thank all of the experts who have appeared before this Chamber, that is you, Mrs. Folnegovic and Ms. Zakic. I always forget to call you all Professors. But you certainly -- that has got nothing to do with my appreciation of your professional skills. Ms. Najman, Mr. Ortakov, Mr. Blagojevic, Ms. Krajinovic, and Mr. Goreta, thank you very much for coming. I wish you a safe trip home again. The Chamber will, after it has received further submissions, will give its decisions in due course. We stand adjourned sine die.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.28 p.m.
